personas.name: The headline-fare traveler
personas.context: An occasional leisure traveler booking a round-trip economy flight for one adult, starting from the advertised headline fare and expecting that number to be close to what they will actually pay.
goals: Book the cheapest workable round-trip for their dates
Know the real, all-in total before entering payment details
Avoid overpaying by picking the wrong fare tier
frustrations: The headline fare excludes carry-on, seat selection, and checked bags, and that only becomes clear deep in the flow
The cheapest-looking fare can end up costing more than a higher tier once seats and bags are added
The same charge is shown differently on different screens, so no number feels reliable
Add-ons arrive with pre-checked boxes and decline options hidden as text links
personas.quote: that $361.79 is not what this trip costs if you're a normal traveler.
grounded_in: True cost hidden in skippable panels
Price levers aren't the default view

personas.name: The fare-structure scrutinizer
personas.context: An experienced traveler who opens the fare-class panel instead of skimming past it, and who weighs trade-offs like a split-airline itinerary before committing to a flight.
goals: Keep full visibility into the fare structure and change/refund rules
Avoid itineraries that split delay risk across two airlines
Control which airports and which fare class are actually in play
frustrations: The search form resists correction: it pre-fills the wrong origin from geolocation and appends instead of replacing typed text
The return leg switches to showing deltas and silently re-prices the already-chosen outbound
The cheapest return option quietly produces a mixed-carrier itinerary without flagging the risk
personas.quote: that would have made it a mixed-carrier itinerary, where a delay on one airline isn't the other's problem.
grounded_in: Search form defaults fight the user
True cost hidden in skippable panels
Price levers aren't the default view

actions: Clear the geolocation-filled origin and retype the real departure city
Choose 'All Airports' for the origin instead of a single airport
Set destination, round-trip, economy, and dates
friction: Origin field pre-filled with the wrong city and appends rather than replaces typed input
Single-airport default would silently narrow results unless the traveler knows to pick 'All Airports'

actions: Read the flexible-dates strip to compare prices across nearby days
Read the left sidebar to work out what the fare tiers include
Consider re-sorting the list by price
friction: Results default to 'Recommended' sort, not price
The real price structure (carry-on and seat cost extra) is disclosed only in the sidebar
Same route, same week, prices swing from $172 to over $1,000 depending on the day

actions: Click a flight and open the fare-class panel
Compare Base vs Main vs premium and flexible tiers
Pick the cheapest fare to see what it really includes
friction: The fare-class panel is the step people skim past
The cheap fare's true cost (seat extra, change fee) is not obvious at the point of choosing it

actions: Read return options priced as deltas rather than totals
Notice a '+$0' option on a different airline and weigh the trade-off
Pick a same-airline return and absorb the added cost
friction: Pricing model switches from totals to deltas without explanation
The cheapest delta would create a mixed-carrier itinerary
Choosing a nicer fare here silently re-prices the outbound leg

actions: Hit a full-screen 'Bundle & Save' flight-plus-car interstitial
Look for a way past it
Click the 'No thanks' text link
friction: 'No thanks' is a text link under the blue button rather than an equal option

actions: Open the seat map and scroll looking for a free seat
Check checked-bag pricing
Decide whether to continue without bags
friction: Every seat on the fare costs $36-$94; there is no free seat even at the back
Checked bags read '$95 roundtrip' here but '$49' per direction on the fare panel
The 'Continue without bags?' dialog wrongly says the trip has no carry-on

actions: Enter name, gender, date of birth, contact details, and billing address
Make the forced trip-insurance choice
Read the fine print and confirm the booking
friction: Trip insurance is a forced choice with a self-incriminating decline: 'I understand my ... booking won't be protected'
Fine print: nonrefundable, $150/ticket change fee, with free cancellation only within 24 hours

hmw_statements.statement: How might we help a traveler see the price they will actually pay before they commit to a fare?
How might we surface the choices that most affect price so a traveler does not miss them by accepting the defaults?
How might we keep cost information consistent and trustworthy as a traveler moves through the booking?
How might we let a traveler weigh a cheaper option against its trade-offs, such as a split-airline itinerary?
How might we give a traveler a clear, pressure-free way to decline add-ons they do not want?
